findings:
🟠 [wdog-scope-empty-fallback-fails-closed] MUST-FIX In `_watchdog_worker_alive` the SCOPE_UNIT branch does not fail open when ps is unusable and WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID is empty: `ps -o state= -p "$rp"` yields empty st (treated as unknown, falls through), then `_watchdog_pgid_has_live ""` hits `[ -n "$target" ] || return 1` before its own ps/unknown check and returns dead, so the watchdog subshell exits at `if ! _watchdog_worker_alive; then exit 0` without ever calling `systemctl --user kill` (which needs no ps at all). WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID is empty exactly on hosts where ps/_self_pgid already failed at launch (selfpg empty) or where `set -m` did not isolate the systemd-run job, so a cgroup-rail run on a host with broken/missing procps gets no wall enforcement while emit/manifest still report `timeout_enforced: true`. This is the Round-2 obligation case and `assert_r6_alive_check_fails_open_to_firing` deliberately sets WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID=12345, so it is untested. Smallest fix: in the SCOPE_UNIT branch, after the state probe, add `if [ -z "$st" ] && [ -z "${WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID:-}" ]; then return 0; fi` (unknown counts as alive; a false fire on a gone scope is un-stamped because `systemctl kill` on an unloaded unit fails and `.fired` is removed), and add a third case to the r6 test with SCOPE_UNIT set, ps stubbed to fail, and WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID unset expecting rc 0.

Not introduced by this diff, own-child only, excluded.
